verses.text: Di song of songs, wey be Solomon own.
Make im kiss me with di kisses of im mouth, because your love sweet pass wine.
Your perfumes smell sweet. Your name be like perfume wey dem pour out. Na why di young women love you.
Draw me after you and make we run. Di king don bring me enter im rooms. We go rejoice and dey glad for you. We go praise your love more pass wine. Dem dey right to love you.
I dark, but I fine, una daughters of Jerusalem, like di tents of Kedar, like di curtains of Solomon.
No look me say I dark, because di sun don look me. My mama pikin dem vex with me. Dem make me keeper of di vineyards, but my own vineyard I no keep.
Tell me, you wey my soul love, wia you dey feed your flock, wia you dey make dem rest for afternoon? Because why I go be like person wey cover face beside di flocks of your friends?
If you no know, you wey fine pass all women, follow di tracks of di flock, and feed your young goats beside di shepherds tents.
I don compare you, my love, to horse for Pharaoh chariots.
Your cheeks fine with rows of jewels, your neck with chains of gold.
We go make you gold ornaments with studs of silver.
While di king dey sit for im table, my perfume dey send out im smell.
My beloved na bundle of myrrh to me, wey dey lie between my breasts.
My beloved na cluster of henna blossoms to me, for di vineyards of En Gedi.
Look, you fine, my love. Look, you fine. Your eyes na doves.
Look, you fine, my beloved, yes, sweet. Our bed dey green.
Di beams of our house na cedar, and our rafters na fir.
I be rose of Sharon, lily of di valleys.
As lily among thorns, so my love dey among di young women.
As apple tree among di trees of di forest, so my beloved dey among di young men. I delight to sit under im shade, and im fruit sweet for my mouth.
E bring me to di banquet hall, and im banner over me na love.
Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples, because I dey sick with love.
Im left hand dey under my head, and im right hand dey embrace me.
I charge una, una daughters of Jerusalem, by di gazelles and by di does of di field, make una no stir up or awaken love until e ready.
Na my beloved voice! Look, e dey come, e dey leap over di mountains, e dey skip over di hills.
My beloved be like gazelle or young deer. Look, e dey stand behind our wall. E dey look through di windows, e dey peep through di lattice.
My beloved talk to me say, “Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
Because look, di winter don pass, di rain don finish and go.
Di flowers dey appear for di land, di time of singing don come, and di voice of di turtledove dey hear for our land.
Di fig tree dey ripen im figs, and di vines dey bloom and dey give sweet smell. Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
My dove, for di clefts of di rock, for di hiding place of di cliff, make I see your face, make I hear your voice, because your voice sweet and your face lovely.”
Catch di foxes for us, di little foxes wey dey spoil di vineyards, because our vineyards dey bloom.
My beloved na my own and I be im own. E dey feed im flock among di lilies.
Until di day break and di shadows run go, turn, my beloved, and be like gazelle or like young deer upon di mountains of Bether.
For night for my bed I seek am wey my soul love. I seek am but I no find am.
I talk say, “I go rise now and go about di city, for di streets and for di squares. I go seek am wey my soul love.” I seek am but I no find am.
Di watchmen wey dey go about di city find me. I ask, “Una don see am wey my soul love?”
I just pass dem small when I find am wey my soul love. I hold am and I no let am go, until I bring am enter my mama house, enter di room of she wey born me.
I charge una, una daughters of Jerusalem, by di gazelles and by di does of di field, make una no stir up or awaken love until e ready.
Who be dis wey dey come up from di wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all di powders of di merchant?
Look, na Solomon litter! 60 mighty men dey around am, of di mighty men of Israel.
Dem all hold sword, dem trained for war. Every man get im sword for im thigh, because of fear for night.
King Solomon make for himself one carriage of di wood of Lebanon.
E make im posts of silver, im back of gold, im seat of purple, im inside dey inlaid with love by di daughters of Jerusalem.
Go out, una daughters of Zion, and behold King Solomon, wearing di crown wey im mama crown am with for di day of im wedding, for di day of di gladness of im heart.
Look, you fine, my love. Look, you fine. Your eyes behind your veil na doves. Your hair be like flock of goats wey dey go down from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth be like flock of sheep wey dem don shear, wey dey come up from di washing, wey every one get twins, and none among dem lose pikin.
Your lips be like thread of scarlet, and your mouth lovely. Your cheeks behind your veil be like piece of pomegranate.
Your neck be like David tower wey dem build for armoury, wey 1,000 shields hang for am, all di shields of mighty men.
Your two breasts be like two fawns, twins of gazelle, wey dey feed among di lilies.
Until di day break and di shadows run go, I go go to di mountain of myrrh and to di hill of frankincense.
You fine all over, my love. No spot dey for you.
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from di top of Amana, from di top of Senir and Hermon, from di dens of lions, from di mountains of leopards.
You don steal my heart, my sister, my bride. You don steal my heart with one look from your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
How fine your love be, my sister, my bride! How much better your love pass wine, and di smell of your perfumes pass all spices!
Your lips, my bride, dey drop honeycomb. Honey and milk dey under your tongue, and di smell of your garments be like di smell of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, na garden wey dem lock, spring wey dem shut up, fountain wey dem seal.
Your shoots na orchard of pomegranates, with choice fruits, henna with nard plants,
nard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense, myrrh and aloes, with all di best spices.
You na fountain for gardens, well of living water, and streams from Lebanon.
Wake up, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow upon my garden, make im spices flow out. Make my beloved come into im garden and eat im choice fruits.

I don come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I don gather my myrrh with my spice. I don eat my honeycomb with my honey. I don drink my wine with my milk. Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink plenty, lovers!

I sleep, but my heart dey awake. Na di voice of my beloved! E dey knock, say, “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one, because my head don full with dew, and my hair with di drops of di night.”
I don comot my robe. How I go put am on again? I don wash my feet. How I go dirty dem again?
My beloved put im hand through di hole for di door, and my heart dey stir for am.
I rise up to open for my beloved, and my hands dey drip with myrrh, and my fingers with flowing myrrh, upon di handles of di lock.
I open for my beloved, but my beloved don turn away and don go. My soul faint when e talk. I seek am, but I no find am. I call am, but e no answer me.
Di watchmen wey dey go about di city find me. Dem beat me and wound me. Di keepers of di walls take my cloak from me.
I charge una, una daughters of Jerusalem, if una find my beloved, wetin una go tell am? Say I dey sick with love.
Wetin your beloved be pass another beloved, you fairest among women? Wetin your beloved be pass another beloved, say you charge us so?
My beloved dey radiant and ruddy, di most distinguished among 10,000.
Im head na most pure gold. Im hair dey wavy, black like raven.
Im eyes be like doves beside streams of water, washed with milk, and dem set well.
Im cheeks be like bed of spices, like banks of sweet herbs. Im lips be like lilies, dey drop flowing myrrh.
Im hands be like rods of gold set with beryl. Im body be like polished ivory overlaid with sapphires.
Im legs be like pillars of marble set on bases of fine gold. Im appearance be like Lebanon, excellent as di cedars.
Im mouth sweet pass anything. Yes, e lovely pass all. Dis na my beloved, and dis na my friend, una daughters of Jerusalem.
Wia your beloved go, you fairest among women? Which way your beloved turn go, make we seek am with you?
My beloved don go down to im garden, to di beds of spices, to feed im flock for di gardens and to gather lilies.
I be my beloved own, and my beloved na my own. E dey feed im flock among di lilies.
You fine like Tirzah, my love, lovely like Jerusalem, awesome like army wey carry banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, because dem don overcome me. Your hair be like flock of goats wey dey go down from Gilead.
Your teeth be like flock of ewes wey dey come up from di washing, wey every one get twins, and none among dem lose pikin.
Your cheeks behind your veil be like piece of pomegranate.
Dere dey 60 queens, 80 concubines, and young women wey no get number.
My dove, my perfect one, na only one she be, di only one of her mama, di pure one of she wey born am. Di young women see am and call am blessed. Yes, di queens and di concubines, and dem praise am.
“Who be dis wey dey look out like di dawn, fair as di moon, clear as di sun, awesome as army wey carry banners?”
I go down to di nut orchard to see di fresh growth of di valley, to see whether di vine don bud, and whether di pomegranates don bloom.
Before I know am, my desire don put me among di chariots of my noble people.
Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, make we look you. Why una go look di Shulammite, as for di dance of Mahanaim?
How beautiful your feet dey for sandals, prince daughter! Di curves of your thighs be like jewels, di work of di hands of skilled craftsman.
Your navel na round goblet wey mixed wine no dey lack. Your waist na heap of wheat wey lilies surround.
Your two breasts be like two fawns, twins of gazelle.
Your neck be like tower of ivory. Your eyes be like di pools for Heshbon, by di gate of Bath Rabbim. Your nose be like di tower of Lebanon wey dey look toward Damascus.
Your head upon you be like Carmel, and di hair of your head like purple. Di king dey captive for di tresses.
How fair and how pleasant you be, love, for delights!
Dis your stature be like palm tree, and your breasts like clusters of fruit.
I talk say, “I go climb up di palm tree. I go hold im fruit.” Make your breasts be like clusters of di vine, di smell of your breath like apples,
and your mouth like di best wine, wey dey go down smooth for my beloved, dey flow over di lips of those wey sleep.
I be my beloved own, and im desire dey toward me.
Come, my beloved, make we go out into di field. Make we stay for di villages.
Make we rise early go di vineyards. Make we see whether di vine don bud, whether di blossom don open, and whether di pomegranates don bloom. Dere I go give you my love.
Di mandrakes dey give smell, and for our doors dey all kinds of choice fruits, new and old, wey I don keep for you, my beloved.
Oh, say you be like my brother, wey suck my mama breasts! When I find you outside, I go kiss you, and dem no go despise me.
I go lead you and bring you enter my mama house, wey go teach me. I go give you spiced wine to drink, di juice of my pomegranate.
Im left hand dey under my head, and im right hand dey embrace me.
I charge una, una daughters of Jerusalem, make una no stir up or awaken love until e ready.
Who be dis wey dey come up from di wilderness, wey dey lean on her beloved? Under di apple tree I wake you up. Dere your mama bring you forth. Dere she wey born you bring you forth.
Set me as seal upon your heart, as seal upon your arm, because love strong like death, jealousy hard like Sheol. Im flashes na flashes of fire, di very flame of di Lord.
Many waters no fit quench love, neither floods fit drown am. If man give all di wealth of im house for love, e go totally dey despised.
We get one small sister, and she never get breasts. Wetin we go do for our sister for di day wey dem go speak for her?
If she be wall, we go build on top of her one silver tower. If she be door, we go enclose her with cedar boards.
I be wall, and my breasts like towers. Den I become for im eyes like one wey find peace.
Solomon get vineyard for Baal Hamon. E give di vineyard to keepers. Everyone go bring 1,000 pieces of silver for im fruit.
My own vineyard, wey na mine, dey before me. You, Solomon, go get di 1,000, and di keepers of di fruit go get 200.
You wey dey live for di gardens, di companions dey listen for your voice. Make I hear am!
Hurry, my beloved, and be like gazelle or like young deer upon di mountains of spices.
